newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures tumble by daily price limits.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures tumble by daily price limits.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures ended sharply lower on Tuesday, with all months except for the spot September contract down by their daily 600 yen limits, traders said.
Forecasts for wetter weather in the U.S. Midwest this weekend pushed down corn futures from the outset, and the weaker CBOT project A trading helped expand the early losses in the afternoon.
The benchmark July 1998 contract was down 600 yen at 14,690 yen per tonne. Activity was buoyant on heavy selling pressure with estimated volume at 94,680 lots.
"Direction hinges on the weather in the U.S. If there is rain as expected, more falls are likely," one trader said. He pegged the support level for the benchmark July at 13,000 yen.
Another trader said the fall was partly in a move to correct the recent price rises here on concerns over dry weather earlier in the United States.
The spot September corn contract on the CBOT Project A trading system was trading at $2.61-1/4 per bushel at 0807 GMT, against $2.63-3/4 at Monday's close.
Spot August CBOT soybean futures on the overnight trading system were at $7.60 per bushel at 0807 GMT, against $7.65-1/4 at Monday's close.
